deficits.evidence: The footway is an informal path blocked by stalls and merchandise.
deficits.suggestion: Construct a dedicated, unobstructed sidewalk on the right side to separate pedestrians from vehicle traffic.

deficits.evidence: Market stalls and goods completely block the pedestrian area.
deficits.suggestion: Relocate market stalls to a designated vending area to clear the pedestrian path.

deficits.evidence: Uneven ground and debris from stalls create trip hazards.
deficits.suggestion: Level the surface and repair the pavement on the right side to remove trip hazards.

deficits.evidence: High pedestrian demand due to shops on both sides, but no designated crossing facility.
deficits.suggestion: Install a marked zebra crossing to provide pedestrians with a safe place to cross the street.

deficits.evidence: Pedestrians are crossing randomly in the carriageway without any safety infrastructure.
deficits.suggestion: Implement a formal crossing point with clear signage to improve pedestrian safety.

ratings.reason: The right side lacks a formal, separated footway, though a generic solution is provided.
Stalls clearly obstruct the pedestrian area on the right.
The ground surface on the right appears uneven and cluttered with debris.
No designated crossing is visible despite high pedestrian activity.
Pedestrians are seen crossing the carriageway haphazardly.
